In general, the problem with unemployment is not that there are no jobs. That's bullshit. there are many jobs and there are the people who could do the jobs. The problem is that the unemployed and the businesses with vacancies don't always find each other.

In Germany, we have this state-run thing called "Jobbörse" (literally "employment stock exchange"). Instead of finding a price two parties agree on, like on a normal stock exchange, this stock exchange is designed to find a set of skills two parties agree on. It's a web service where all workers, unemployed or not, can register themselves and create a profile with their skills and career ambitions. Likewise, businesses can create profiles listing their vacancies and the skills that they would like in their employee-to-be. While each can do their own search for matches, it is the job of the state agency that runs the jobbörse to find suitable matches and recommend them to the unemployed and the businesses. If you declare yourself unemployed at the state employment agency, you HAVE to report your carrer, your education, and your skill set for the jobbörse. if you don't already have a profile, one will be created for you.

And if you have completed one of the many [legally recognized work trainings](http://mkenyaujerumani.de/2013/06/22/understanding-the-concept-of-a-german-ausbildung-vocational-training/) and still can't find employment, the state will cover conversion training for you that would normally be around several thousand euros. (in the long run, this is cheaper for the state than providing unemployment benefits until the worker can improve their skillset themselves) this includes special driver's licenses, programming languages, and even some certificates.

if you have just completed or dropped out of your mandatory public school education and cannot find a vocational training job, the state will put you in special education courses that are designed to feel like a mix of job and school. the aim is to fill gaps in your education, prevent you from becoming lazy and having a big gap in your CV, tell you how to write a CV and get you into internships for your CV. by the time this course finishes for you (after one year) you are very likely to have already signed a contract for vocational training.

i myself found myself out of work after my software developer traineeship, and the state helped me by covering my conversion training to learn a programming language that is actually used. They found me an amazing business to work at, full of wonderful people.

while you could argue that a private agency can do all this, too, i think it's better to have an official, central place for this purpose. And while everyone clamors for the government to do something about unemployment, this one has something **besides** infrastructure projects.

i'm interested to learn how this is done in other countries. Does your country do something similar? Does your country do something better? Does your country not do this and you think this is a good idea?
